explanation: N740+ is a retrospective lexical detector for the learned Graeco-Latin vocabulary of expository scholarly, technical and legal prose: it fires when the current token is one of that register's argument words - abstract nouns and relational adjectives such as theory, hypothesis, method, technique, principle, theorem, paradigm, aspect, invention, literature, evidence, equivalent, analogous, suitable, ideal - or a piece of such a word (' matics' in Mathematics, 'ry' in Freemasonry, 'odynamics' in Thermodynamics), and it stays at or below zero on the commonest everyday Germanic vocabulary (cat, dog, garden, hammer, bottle, good, big, nice, tall all give z = 0). Weaker firings follow the same style through its grammaticalized words (the particle in 'carried out'/'broke down', the auxiliary in 'studies have', the participle in 'is known'), and a minority of plain everyday words (glue, dream, hope, soft) do reach 0.3-1.0, so this is a lexical-register class rather than a clean concreteness split.
